title: The adoption kit for the main product
request: Give the main product a way to adopt dclab_core: its outputs mapped field by field onto the main product's contracts, a versioned wheel with a changelog, and a guide naming each call site, without copying or importing the main product.
spec: dclab_core as a versioned wheel with a changelog; dclab_core.adapters.main_product mapping each output onto ProblemSpec content, ProblemProfile, MetricPlan, HoldoutPlan, ValidationPlan, ExperimentPlan per decision point and Objective, from recorded field lists; docs/guides/CORE_INTEGRATION.md with the call sites, the Advisor over its gateway, what never crosses, and the tests it should add. Done when the wheel installs in a clean Python 3.12 with only its dependencies, the mapping tests pass against the field lists recorded with the commit read, and the guide names every call site.
plan: Built in an isolated worktree by a sub-agent, fast-forwarded to main first.
Read the main product with gh, read only, at commit 7fa23b9, and record the field lists, the decision-point registry with caps and the vocabularies in main_product_fields.json with the files read.
Write pure mapping functions that return plain JSON with exactly the recorded fields; a field the core cannot fill is None with a note.
Move the library to 0.2.0 with a changelog; write a wheel check that builds with uv, installs in a clean Python 3.12 and solves a replica from an unrelated folder.
Write the guide; run the dclab-reviewer (it re-read the main product at the same commit); fix the 8 findings; rd-check (1,021 tests).

decisions.decision: Field lists are recorded from one commit of the main product; its code is never copied or imported.
decisions.why: The owner's rule; and a test can then check the mapping against what was actually read.

decisions.decision: A field the core cannot fill is None with a note, never a guess.
decisions.why: Examples: no test size, folds or seed (the host's defaults); recall at a budget or top-k have no main-product metric; a time-and-entity split is 'unsupported', as the main product's own planners answer.

decisions.decision: Every plan decision goes through a governed decision point with its cap, or says why none takes it.
decisions.why: The main product adopts proposals through its own governance, never a second pipeline.

decisions.decision: Only out-of-fold training figures cross; target statistics on every row and holdout figures never do.
decisions.why: The main product computes statistics on the training partition only and scores the holdout once.

decisions.decision: The guide splits analysis in two: target-free at load-profile, the target after the holdout lock on the locked training rows.
decisions.why: The text said 'the load-profile stage after the holdout lock', but in the main product load-profile runs before the lock.

change: dclab_core/adapters/main_product.py and main_product_fields.json, dclab_core/CHANGELOG.md and version 0.2.0, scripts/core_wheel_check.py and make core-wheel-check, docs/guides/CORE_INTEGRATION.md; tests/test_core_adapters.py and tests/test_core_wheel.py.

findings.defect: All-row target statistics crossed through problem_profile, labelled as training-row figures.
findings.scenario: problem_profile(analyse({'orders.csv': delivery orders}, target='actual_minutes')) without a training index returned the target's min, max and median with the note '(training rows)' and nothing listed as excluded.
findings.cause: The adapter copied the figures whether or not the findings had a training split.
findings.fix: When the findings have no training rows (or carry the no-split warning), the three target fields are None with a note, and listed as excluded.

findings.defect: The guide's 'target-free' analysis before the holdout lock was not target-free.
findings.scenario: Following the guide, analyse(..., target=None, brief=understand(...)) took the target from the brief and computed the distribution, the cap and leak tests on all rows before the lock.
findings.cause: analyse falls back to the brief's target column.
findings.fix: The guide passes no brief before the lock, and a test asserts no target or leakage finding there.

findings.defect: The guide's call after the lock omitted the training index.
findings.scenario: analyse on the locked training rows without train_index added a spurious no-split warning that the plan turns into a risk and a split citation in every run.
findings.cause: A missing argument in the guide.

findings.defect: The holdout test could not catch a holdout figure crossing.
findings.scenario: The test only searched for the word 'holdout'; copying the holdout precision into the threshold fields would have passed, since in the budget case both precisions were 1.0.
findings.cause: A test of names, not of values.
findings.fix: An invariance test: run assess twice with different holdout labels and scores and require identical threshold fields and notes.

findings.defect: An inferred target crossed without a note.
findings.scenario: experiment_plan took the brief's target column whenever known, including when it was only inferred, though the target is an answer a person must give.
findings.cause: The status of the fact was not read.
findings.fix: An inferred target is flagged: 'inferred, not stated; a person confirms it'.

findings.defect: Proposed families could get the host's whole families answer refused.
findings.scenario: gradient_boosting expanded to xgboost, lightgbm and catboost from the recorded portfolio; on a host without catboost the main product refuses the whole answer as a family not in its portfolio.
findings.cause: The adapter assumed the host's installed families.
findings.fix: The guide and the function say the host intersects the list with its own portfolio before submitting; the note explains the same-named sklearn family.

findings.defect: holdout_plan gave the wrong 'stratified' for an unsupported split.
findings.scenario: For a time-and-entity split it returned stratified False, while the main product's planner returns stratified for classification tasks in that case, and the adapter's own validation_plan already did.
findings.cause: Two functions mirrored the host differently.
findings.fix: stratified = classification when the strategy is unsupported.

findings.defect: The ProblemSpec's JSON size limit was not checked.
findings.scenario: The main product refuses constraints or success criteria over 16 KB; the adapter put every brief constraint and criterion in unbounded, so a long brief would be answered with a 422.
findings.fix: Record the limit and leave over-limit fields to a person with a note.

measurements.name: the wheel in a clean Python 3.12
measurements.gate: The wheel builds and installs in a clean Python 3.12 with only its dependencies (Done-when of 17.8).
measurements.result: Wheel 0.2.0 built with uv, installed with only its dependency closure (numpy 2.5.4, pandas 3.0.6, scikit-learn 1.9.1, pydantic 2.14.1), no unexpected packages, and solved the delivery replica from an unrelated folder in about 80 s; the reviewer re-ran it and it passed.

measurements.name: the mapping against the recorded field lists
measurements.gate: Every output has exactly the recorded fields in plain JSON, every gap explained, on the three replicas.
measurements.result: Passes; the acceptance proposals map as expected (fraud: group-disjoint by biker, StratifiedGroupKFold, pr_auc; tickets: temporal_future; delivery: GroupKFold by restaurant, mae).

outcome: Done: dclab_core 0.2.0 as a wheel with a changelog, its outputs mapped field by field onto the main product's contracts at a recorded commit, and a guide naming each call site; 8 review findings fixed. Wiring is the main repository's own change. Open: before the lock the core reads no target, so its split proposal there is weaker; per-role output schemas; the main product's improve loop is not built yet.
lessons: An integration guide is code: a wrong argument in it (a brief before the lock) leaks as surely as a bug.
Test that holdout figures do not cross by changing the holdout and checking nothing moves, not by searching for a word.
Record the other system's limits (sizes, portfolios) with its field lists, or valid output gets refused there.
